title: Two open milestones share the same title, and nothing ever flags it
author: off-by-one
description: Groups the repository's own milestones by exact, trimmed title: when two or more currently-open milestones carry the byte-identical title, the same body of work is being tracked in two places at once. Unlike duplicate-issue-still-open and duplicate-pr-still-open, which watch an explicit 'duplicate of #N' prose promise that GitHub gives no auto-close wiring for, milestones carry no such convention -- the seam here is structural: GitHub enforces no uniqueness constraint on milestone titles at all, so a re-created, forgotten-then-repeated milestone can sit alongside its twin indefinitely with no warning anywhere.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the later (duplicate) milestone has existed while both it and the earlier one with the identical title stay open -- not flat. Under 24 hours since the duplicate was created scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- a human may be mid-cleanup, about to close or rename one of the two within the day). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal, two open milestones with the exact same title. The 24h window matches duplicate-issue-still-open's and duplicate-pr-still-open's own bar rather than inventing a new number for a structurally similar family. A title held by only one milestone, or by two-plus milestones where fewer than two currently read open, is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the identical discipline every recipe before this one holds.
